clue.text: Loiter around an interesting German city

indicators.note: around tells us the loitering word wraps itself about the little word an

parts.note: to loiter is to hover, hang about

explanation.surface: Someone idles about a German city they find interesting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interesting' only colours the surface; the definition is just the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanover (Hannover) is a city in Lower Saxony, northern Germany.

clue.text: He will shortly get his punishment, it's awful

parts.note: he will, contracted, is he'll

indicators.note: the word his is punished, knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer is about to be punished, and it's dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punishment' is an unusual anagram signal: the three letters are beaten into a new order; the contraction's apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hellish is dreadful, as unpleasant as the inferno.

clue.text: One of the gears in a new Renault

indicators.note: new signals that the car maker's name is made anew in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A gear position on a brand-new French car.
explanation.definitionFit: Neutral is the gearbox position in which no drive is engaged.

clue.text: Six ride pointlessly, they're very green

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: without a point: E, a compass point, is taken away from the word ride

explanation.surface: Novice cyclists ride aimlessly, being very inexperienced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointlessly' removes E (east, a compass point) from RIDE, leaving RID.
explanation.definitionFit: Virid is a literary word for a vivid verdant colour.

clue.text: Rub a party member with surgical scraper

parts.note: to rasp is to rub roughly
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Someone scrapes a politician with a medical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A raspatory is a file-like surgical tool used to scrape bone.

clue.text: Elevation-but no elevator!

explanation.surface: A rocket rises, though no lift is involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Liftoff is a rocket's rising from the pad; read as two words it says the lift (British for elevator) is not working.

clue.text: I sell twisted cotton thread

indicators.note: twisted tells us the letters of I sell are wound into another order

explanation.surface: A merchant explains they sell twisted yarn.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, strong, tightly spun cotton yarn, used for stockings.

clue.text: At liberty to turn to coast

parts.note: someone at liberty is free
to wheel is to turn round

explanation.surface: A freed person decides to head for the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: To coast on a bicycle is to ride without pedalling.

clue.text: The final one to go-and keep going

parts.note: out means gone, departed
the final one is the last

explanation.surface: Someone is the last to leave and carries on regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlast is to survive or endure longer than others.

clue.text: Opens up first class fragrant bloom

parts.note: frees, as in opens up or releases

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters climb, so they are read bottom to top

parts.note: A1 means first class, with the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A first-class scented flower opens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns A1, read AI, into IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Freesias are sweet-smelling flowering plants from southern Africa.

clue.text: Windows fitted at the French national museum?

definitions.text: Windows fitted at the French national museum?

parts.words: Windows fitted at the French national museum?
parts.note: the Paris art gallery's name, made plural, would fit glazing put in there

explanation.surface: A question about glazing installed in the Paris gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Louvres are slatted openings or shutters admitting air, and the Louvre is the national museum in Paris.

clue.text: Somehow respect one who gives a fright

indicators.note: somehow suggests the word respect is put together in some other way

explanation.surface: Someone frightening is still, somehow, respected.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectre is a ghost or phantom that frightens people.

clue.text: Annoyed about bungled raid, so blaze out

indicators.note: about tells us the cross word goes round the other piece

parts.note: annoyed means irate

indicators.note: bungled means the raid letters are botched into a jumble

explanation.surface: Angry after a failed raid, someone sets fires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bungled' makes RADI, which 'about' sets in the middle of the angry word, splitting it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To irradiate is to shine or radiate light upon something.

clue.text: Is all dressed up, but may swear!

indicators.note: may hints that the swear word could take another form when rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone smartly attired might still use bad language.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wears clothes has them on, is dressed in them.

clue.text: Stops at very small stations

explanation.surface: A train pauses at tiny railway stops.
explanation.definitionFit: Halts are stops, and in Britain a halt is also a tiny unstaffed railway stop.

clue.text: Weakening on the point of getting fit

parts.note: S is south, a compass point
training is getting fit through exercise

explanation.surface: An athlete is fading just as they get into shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Straining a joint or rope overstretches and so weakens it.

clue.text: Wild carthorse scattered the band

indicators.note: scattered means the carthorse letters are dispersed and regathered

explanation.surface: A runaway horse scatters the musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' rearranges CARTHORSE; 'Wild' only adds to the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large group of musicians playing together.

clue.text: Seamen from Eire are good at opening bottles

definitions.text: Seamen from Eire are good at opening bottles

parts.words: Seamen from Eire are good at opening bottles
parts.note: sailors of an Irish port's ship, its crew, give the name of a wine-opening tool

explanation.surface: Irish sailors are handy at uncorking drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Cork is a port and county in the Republic of Ireland (Eire); its ship's company is Cork's crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A corkscrew is the spiral tool used to draw stoppers from wine bottles.

clue.text: One who makes a picture of carrier holding bean

indicators.note: holding means the carrier word clasps the other piece within it

parts.note: a porter carries luggage
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: An artist depicts a luggage carrier with a shaft of light.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper text has been read as 'bean'; the wordplay needs a shaft of light, so 'beam' is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray is to depict, so this is a depicter or painter.

clue.text: Add afterthought to change a book

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is an afterthought at the end of a letter
to alter is to change

explanation.surface: A writer tacks on a note in order to revise a volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalter is a volume containing the Psalms.

clue.text: Train driver involved in alarm

indicators.note: involved means the letters of in and alarm are tangled together

explanation.surface: An engine driver is caught up in an emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: A railman is a railway worker, such as one who drives locomotives.

clue.text: An inn nearby

explanation.surface: There is a pub close at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a local is one's neighbourhood pub; as an adjective it means close by.

clue.text: Warm drink?

explanation.surface: A question about a hot beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordial means friendly and heartfelt, and a cordial is a sweet fruit drink.

clue.text: Medical men who take blood

explanation.surface: Doctors who draw blood from patients.
explanation.definitionFit: Leech was an old word for a physician, and leeches are worms that suck blood.

clue.text: This proved I was in Bali getting cooked at the time!

definitions.text: This proved I was in Bali getting cooked at the time!

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are mixed up as if stirred in a pan

explanation.surface: Someone claims their sunburn proves they were away in Bali.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is proof of being elsewhere when a crime happened.

clue.text: The sermon record belongs to us, we get a point

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
something that belongs to us is ours
E is east, a compass point

explanation.surface: A preacher lays claim to a recording and makes a point.
explanation.definitionFit: A discourse is a formal spoken treatment of a subject, such as a lecture or homily.

clue.text: Nudes might go sunbathing R here

indicators.note: might go hints that the nudes letters could move into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Naturists may head to the sandhills to sunbathe.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunes are sandy hills behind a beach, a sheltered spot for lying in the sun.

clue.text: Circular tour-or part of it

parts.note: a bit is a part or piece

explanation.surface: A round trip, or just a section of it.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is a path round a planet, a circuit.

clue.text: He worked on time and motion quietly!

definitions.text: He worked on time and motion quietly!

indicators.note: worked on suggests the letters are reworked and reshaped

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A time-and-motion expert went about his job silently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked on' rearranges MOTION plus P. Thomas Tompion was a celebrated English clockmaker of the 17th century, so he worked on time.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Tompion, the father of English clockmaking, built timepieces.

clue.text: Refuse some grub bishop offers

indicators.note: some means only part of the phrase grub bishop is taken

explanation.surface: A clergyman offers food that someone turns down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes the run of letters across 'grub bishop'.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse, stressed on the first syllable, is waste or garbage.

clue.text: Deserts might have green points

indicators.note: might have hints the word green could be rearranged

parts.note: E and S are two compass points, east and south

explanation.surface: Arid lands might have patches of verdure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might have' rearranges GREEN into RENEG, followed by E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To renege is to go back on a promise, as one who abandons a cause.

clue.text: Twigs that the French are after power unit

indicators.note: are after means the French article comes behind the power unit

parts.note: the watt is the unit of power
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: Sticks bound together come after electrical units.
explanation.definitionFit: Wattles are interwoven sticks and branches used for fences and walls.
